newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB shares fall despite restructure plans.
newsitem.headline: NCB shares fall despite restructure plans.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank (NCB) shares fell on Wednesday morning despite its announcement of restructuring plans, brokers said.
As of 0103 GMT, the shares were down five yen at 256. Trade totalled 3.157 million shares, making it the fifth most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Analysts said the NCB restructuring plan was insufficient to solve the bank's big bad-loan problems and would also place an unfortunate burden on stronger, healthier banks.
"Foreign investors especially are sceptical that NCB's restructuring plan and that of Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd are going to be effective," a "Big Four" broker said.
"They may refrain from buying bank sector shares for a while and if they do, there will be little support for the shares in the sector."
